channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Reação de ministro Gilmar turbina Zema e impulsiona engajamento da pauta anti-Supremo
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court’s (STF) reaction to Senator Alessandro Vieira’s request to indict ministers—particularly Justice Gilmar Mendes’ move to include Governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry—has inadvertently amplified political engagement around the anti-Supreme narrative. This response boosted Zema’s visibility and strengthened his confrontation rhetoric, with allies noting recent social media growth. Despite potential reversals, STF justices fear the conflict may become a permanent campaign theme, deepening the Court’s image crisis and prolonging its electoral wear.

item.title: TSE reconhece renúncia de Cláudio Castro em acórdão de julgamento
item.description: The TSE recognized the resignation of Cláudio Castro in a court ruling, declaring him ineligible for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. The decision bars him from running in future elections for eight years.

item.title: Em pleno século 21, Brasil volta aos anos 50 com 'yankees go home' de Lula
item.description: Brazil's Federal Police announced the withdrawal of credentials for a U.S. immigration agent operating in Brazil, framed as retaliation for alleged U.S. actions against Brazilian interests. The incident, occurring on Wednesday the 22nd, was characterized by analysts as a 'yankees go home' political move, evoking historical tensions over national sovereignty. The action reflects Lula’s more assertive foreign policy stance, aligned with narratives of independence and resistance to external pressure.

item.title: Enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro se omite, Zema enfrenta o STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is criticized for his silence amid STF investigations into the so-called 'Coup Plot,' while Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema directly confronts the Supreme Federal Court in judicial matters. Despite his rhetoric of opposing the 'system,' Flávio Bolsonaro did not take a public stance of defiance or confrontation during his father’s testimony, contrasting with Zema’s approach. The piece highlights the inconsistency between Bolsonarist rhetoric of resistance and the practice of silence or evasion under institutional pressure.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão que condena ex-governador Cláudio Castro e confirma renúncia
item.description: The TSE published a ruling confirming the ineligibility of former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, but found his cassation moot due to his prior resignation. Rio de Janeiro opted for an indirect election via the state legislature (Alerj) for the interim governorship, and the matter was referred to the STF to determine the selection model, after Justice Flávio Dino requested more time to review the case.

item.title: Lula passa por dois procedimentos médicos no Sírio-Libanês nesta sexta em SP
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva undergoes two medical procedures at São Paulo's Sírio-Libanês Hospital on Friday, the 24th: a scalp cauterization to treat keratosis and an infiltration in his right thumb for tendinitis. The Secretariat of Social Communication (Secom) stated the procedures will not affect his future commitments, and he will remain in São Paulo until Saturday, the 25th, with a planned appearance at the closing of the 8th PT National Congress in Brasília on Sunday, the 26th, pending confirmation the day before.

item.title: Crusoé: O inconfidente
item.description: The article reflects on the commemoration of the Inconfidência Mineira during Tiradentes' holiday, featuring former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema questioning whether Brazilians are truly free today despite historical independence. He links the 18th-century revolt against Portuguese rule to contemporary debates about liberty and governance in Brazil.

item.title: Lula dá entrada em hospital para fazer cauterização na cabeça e infiltração por causa de tendinite na mão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was admitted to the Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital in São Paulo for a cauterization procedure to remove a scalp keratosis and an injection in his right wrist to treat tendonitis. The procedures are quick and routine, with no contraindications, and Lula is expected to rest at home on Friday and Saturday. His attendance at the PT Congress closing in Brasília on Sunday remains unconfirmed, though he has scheduled engagements in the interior of São Paulo on Monday.

item.title: Uma nota da comunidade para o pedido de desculpas de Gilmar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes apologized after referencing homosexuality when referring to Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate. The X community issued a note emphasizing that, per STF rulings (ADO 26 and MI 4.733, June 13, 2019), homophobia and transphobia are equated to crime, framing the apology as consistent with existing jurisprudence.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede desculpas por citar homossexualidade como possível 'acusação injuriosa' contra Zema: 'Errei'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes admitted error for citing homosexuality as a possible 'injurious accusation' against Romeu Zema in a TV Globo interview, later apologizing on X. He defended continuing the fake news inquiry and including Zema in the process, citing a 'defamation industry' against the Court. Opposition lawmakers are articulating a new impeachment request against Mendes following his move to include Zema in the investigation.

item.title: Gilmar cita ideia de fazer ‘boneco de Zema como homossexual’ e diz que seria ofensivo
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes suggested in an interview that making dolls of Governor Romeu Zema as homosexual could be considered an injurious accusation, sparking backlash. He later admitted the error, apologized for equating homosexuality with theft, and vowed to confront what he called a 'defamation industry' against the Court. Zema responded that Mendes oversteps boundaries, that comparing homosexuality to theft reveals prejudice, and shared an AI-generated image of himself holding an LGBTQIA+ flag with a laughing emoji.

item.title: O tiro no pé de Gilmar Mendes
item.description: The dean of the Brazilian Supreme Court, Gilmar Mendes, gave a series of unprecedented interviews this week in an attempt to defend the Court’s image and discredit presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema. His effort backfired, drawing criticism and reinforcing perceptions of bias. The episode was described as a 'self-inflicted wound,' as it further damaged the credibility of both Mendes and the STF.

item.title: MEC Livros terá acervo ampliado para 25 mil obras
item.description: The Ministry of Education expanded the MEC Livros collection from 8,000 to 25,000 works and now allows early return of books after reading 10% or 90% of the content, responding to user demand for greater flexibility. The platform, accessible via Gov.br login, has over 500,000 registered users and offers free borrowing of national and international titles. The announcement was made during the 9º Prêmio Vivaleitura, with President Lula in attendance, who emphasized the importance of accessible reading for all.

item.title: Crise entre Zema e o STF escala e ministro já fala em prisão do ex-governador de Minas
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo party, intensified unfounded criticisms of the STF, prompting Minister Gilmar Mendes to act against him in the Fake News inquiry. STF ministers warn that his attacks could lead to legal consequences, including possible imprisonment, though Zema denies crossing any line and defends the right to criticize public officials, even ironically.

item.title: SobeDesce: de John Ternus ao ChatGPT
item.description: Fifty-year-old executive John Ternus will become Apple's new CEO in September, succeeding Tim Cook. Brazilian swimmer Gabriel Araújo was named Paralympic Athlete of the Year at the Laureus World Sports Awards. Meanwhile, ChatGPT is under investigation by Florida's Attorney General for messages exchanged with a shooter who killed two at a university in 2025; Botafogo received a FIFA transfer ban due to debts, and only 36% of Brazilians consider driving electric vehicles.

item.title: Janja e Michelle ganham protagonismo na corrida pelos votos decisivos das mulheres
item.description: Women represent 51.5% of Brazil's population and 52.8% of the electorate, forming a decisive majority in the 2026 elections despite historical exclusion from top political power. Although Lula still maintains above-average approval among women, his support dropped from 48% to 45% between January and April, and his lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in female voters in second-round simulations fell from 13 to 4 points, signaling erosion of his base. The president has intensified agendas like the national pact against femicide to try to reclaim this crucial electorate.

item.title: O atraso
item.description: Lula seeks to improve his electoral image by reviving rhetoric against U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, attempting to use a confrontation with Trump as a campaign theme to combat his high rejection. Despite initial diplomatic enthusiasm following brief encounters with Trump, no substantive progress was made in bilateral relations, and Washington officials say nothing has changed. Lula tries to draw Trump into the electoral game, but the relationship remains superficial, based on unmet expectations.

item.title: Caso Ramagem põe governo na mira da oposição e abre outra frente de atrito com Trump
item.description: The swift arrest and release of Alexandre Ramagem in the U.S. exposed flaws in Brazil-U.S. international cooperation, drawing criticism from the U.S. State Department over alleged PF manipulation of immigration systems. The incident allowed Ramagem to retaliate by praising Trump-aligned Bolsonarists in the U.S., calling the PF a 'police of thugs,' and prompting opposition demands for PF director Andrei Rodrigues to testify before the Foreign Relations Committee.

item.title: “O inimigo é o PT”, diz Mateus Simões, governador de Minas
item.description: Governor of Minas Gerais, Mateus Simões (PSD), successor of Romeu Zema, states his goal is to defeat the PT in the 2026 elections, despite trailing in polls. He aims to build a triple ticket with Zema, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), but emphasizes loyalty to Zema for selecting him as vice. Simões also highlights his strategy of governing outside Belo Horizonte to strengthen his presence in the interior and connect with the state’s political base.

item.title: PT promove 8º congresso de olho em aliança com a “direita liberal”
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) held its 8th National Congress in Brasília, advocating for an alliance with 'liberal right' forces to counter authoritarian far-right movements, strengthen democracy, and expand its political project. The event paid tribute to founding militants Clara Charf and Sonia Braga and discussed proposals including judicial reform, Armed Forces changes, and updates to the party program.

item.title: PL quer confirmar André do Prado como candidato ao Senado por SP em até 10 dias
item.description: The PL is expected to confirm André do Prado as its Senate candidate for São Paulo within 10 days, with support from Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and approval from Eduardo Bolsonaro following a positive meeting in the U.S. The move aims to finalize the state’s majoritarian ticket alongside Tarcísio, positioning André as a moderate figure to balance the bolsonarist alliance.

item.title: Conselheiro de Trump diz que “brasileiras causam confusão”
item.description: Paolo Zampolli, an advisor to Donald Trump, made offensive remarks about Brazilian women in an Rai interview, claiming they are 'programmed to cause confusion' and referring to his ex-wife Amanda Ungaro and a friend named Lídia with derogatory terms. He also had ties to Jeffrey Epstein and proposed replacing Iran with Italy in the 2026 World Cup. Amanda Ungaro, a Brazilian former model, was deported from the U.S. in 2025 and attributes her removal to Zampolli’s political influence.

item.title: Um terço dos partidos pode ficar sem fundo partidário se repetir desempenho de 2022
item.description: At least 11 of Brazil’s 30 political parties could lose access to the Party Fund and free TV/radio advertising in 2026 if they repeat their 2022 performance, due to a stricter electoral barrier clause. Avante, currently eligible, would be excluded, while the PDT narrowly cleared the threshold. To qualify in 2026, parties must secure 2.5% of national valid votes (with 1.5% in nine states or eight plus DF) or elect at least 13 deputies across nine states (or eight plus DF).

item.title: Lula vai retirar queratose na cabeça; entenda o que é o procedimento
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two simple surgical procedures this Friday at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital: a wrist infiltration to treat thumb tendinitis and removal of a scalp keratosis. Keratosis is a benign skin lesion common in older adults, often removed for aesthetic or preventive reasons, as some types have pre-cancerous potential. The Presidency stated Lula will face no restrictions or need for rest after the procedures.

item.title: Zema se diz melhor que Flávio e Caiado para corrigir erros do PT. Vídeo
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and Novo Party presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema criticized Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes for including him in the fake news inquiry over satirical videos. Zema said Mendes should visit Minas Gerais to learn about his government and accused STF ministers of using their positions to enrich themselves, advocating for their impeachment. He also described the STF as a "Supreme Business Counter" now causing crises in Brazil.

item.title: Zema escala ataque ao STF: "Supremo Balcão de Negócios". Vídeo
item.description: Romeu Zema, pré-candidate of the Novo Party for the Brazilian presidency, accused Supreme Court ministers Dias Toffoli and Alexandre de Moraes of forming a 'Supreme Court of Business' by allegedly associating with Daniel Vorcaro’s Banco Master, claiming they drank whiskey, flew on private jets, and attended parties together. Zema argued they should face impeachment, investigation, and possible imprisonment, claiming the STF has shifted from being a 'firefighter' to an 'arsonist' of Brazilian institutions. He also criticized Justice Gilmar Mendes for including him in the fake news inquiry, calling it persecution and defending his satirical videos as legitimate expression.

item.title: Governo usa R$ 4,5 milhões para organizar acervo privado de Lula em SP
item.description: The federal government has signed an agreement with the UFABC Foundation to organize President Lula's private archive in São Bernardo do Campo, allocating R$ 4.5 million. The project covers transportation, sanitation, technical treatment, cataloging, digitization, and temporary storage of documents, photographs, videos, and bibliographic materials, running from May 2025 to the end of 2026. The Civil House states the measure is supported by Law nº 8.394/1991, which defines such archives as public interest and part of Brazil's cultural heritage.

item.title: Augusto Cury diz que, se eleito presidente, pode acabar com a fome mundial e mediar guerra de Putin e Zelenski: 'Sou especialista em pacificação'
item.description: Augusto Cury, a Brazilian writer and psychiatrist, has launched himself as a pre-candidate for President in the 2026 elections under the Avante party, proposing to mediate international conflicts such as the Russia-Ukraine war and end world hunger by redirecting military spending. He claims expertise in conflict pacification based on his books and suggests creating a global fund using 0.5% of international trade or 2-3% of arms sales to solve hunger.

item.title: Entenda as medidas do governo até agora para reduzir o impacto da guerra no preço dos combustíveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government announced new measures to mitigate the impact of rising international oil prices on fuel costs at Brazilian gas stations. The actions aim to curb price increases and relieve consumer burden, though specific details of the measures were not disclosed in the provided excerpt. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Pré-candidatos ao Planalto defendem mudanças no STF para se blindar ou surfar a crise na Corte
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates for the 2026 election are advocating for reforms to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in response to the crisis stemming from the Master case, either to shield themselves from investigations or to gain political support by attacking the judiciary. The opposition proposes term limits for justices and changes in the appointment process, while the PT plans to include in its party platform a defense of conduct rules for higher courts, aligned with STF President Edson Fachin’s stance. Lula reportedly told Alexandre de Moraes not to allow Justice Daniel Vorcaro’s biography to be discarded.

item.title: Pacto de Lula 3 para retomar obras na educação só concluiu 20% das construções em três anos
item.description: The National Pact for the Resumption of Works, launched by the Lula government in 2023 to complete 5,6 thousand stalled school constructions, has seen only 20% of committed projects finished (753 out of 3,7 thousand adherents) three years later, despite a pledge to allocate nearly R$ 4 billion by 2026. Examples like the daycare in Águas Lindas de Goiás, started in 2013 and halted at 80% completion, illustrate the delay, leaving hundreds of children without spots as structures deteriorate. The program prioritizes advanced, old, and socially vulnerable projects but struggles with implementation despite FNDE’s technical and financial support.

item.title: Enredo manjado ameaça Lula 4
item.description: Polls show a concrete risk of Lula’s defeat in October, prompting PT leaders to seek ways to reconnect the president with the broad front forces of 2022 and renew the alliance on new grounds. However, they struggle to engage these groups around a forward-looking national project, as voters express fatigue with Lula and the perception that the government offers a stale, repetitive narrative.

item.title: Santa Marta congrega a los países que quieren dejar atrás los combustibles fósiles: así llega América Latina a la conferencia
item.description: The Santa Marta International Conference brings together delegates from over 50 countries to discuss transitioning away from fossil fuels, occurring at a paradoxical moment for Latin America. While countries like Colombia, Mexico, and Brazil announce contradictory measures — such as investing in fracking and exploring oil in the Amazon — others see rising oil prices as an opportunity to boost exports. The conference takes place amid the 2026 presidential elections in Brazil, Colombia, and Bolivia, with regional energy policy implications.

item.title: Ministros do STF avaliam que proposta de reforma do Judiciário deve ficar para depois das eleições
item.description: STF ministers believe that the judicial reform proposal presented by Flávio Dino should be postponed until after the 2026 elections, as the electoral climate could hinder the necessary coordination among the three branches. They argue that any broad discussion of the judiciary during this period risks being captured by political disputes and should be deepened only after the election.

item.title: Gilmar oferece escada para tirar Zema do pelotão dos nanicos
item.description: Romeu Zema launched an offensive against the Federal Supreme Court to improve his standing in the 2026 presidential race, but the strategy has not yet affected opinion polls. Despite the lack of electoral impact so far, the movement has recently gained unexpected momentum, possibly due to political or institutional backing. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Governo Lula deve lançar ‘novo Desenrola’ em 1º de maio
item.description: The Lula government plans to launch a new debt renegotiation program, dubbed the 'new Desenrola,' on May 1st, Workers' Day, to boost the president's popularity. The proposal is still under discussion, with final details expected to be settled next week, according to sources speaking to GLOBO. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Zema diz que Gilmar compara homossexual com ladrão
item.description: Romeu Zema, a presidential pre-candidate from Novo, accused Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes of showing prejudice after Mendes questioned whether portraying Zema as a homosexual puppet was offensive in his satire series 'Os Intocáveis'. Zema replied that 'only offends when there is a kernel of truth' and said he has a 'clear conscience', following Mendes' apology for referencing homosexuality, while maintaining his criticism of the satirical videos. The controversy is part of a broader legal move where Mendes requested an investigation into Zema for alleged fake news, prompting the PGR to review the videos under seal.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes diz que errou ao citar homossexualidade em críticas a Zema
item.description: Justice Gilmar Mendes admitted he erred by linking homosexuality to an accusation against Romeu Zema in a Metrópoles interview, later apologizing. The incident occurred amid Mendes’ request to include Zema in the fake news investigation, based on a video where Zema criticizes the STF, portraying justices as puppets. Zema said he was not notified and criticized the STF’s lack of due process in secretive investigations.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão de julgamento que condenou Castro e reconhece renúncia do ex-governador
item.description: The TSE published the ruling that convicted former governor Cláudio Castro of abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, declaring him ineligible for eight years, but recognized that the vacancy of the office was due to resignation, not cassation of the diploma. This leaves open the method for selecting the interim governor in Rio de Janeiro, currently under the responsibility of the TJ-RJ president, as the final decision rests with the STF, where Minister Flávio Dino is still reviewing the case.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão de julgamento que condenou Cláudio Castro
item.description: The TSE published the ruling that condemned former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) to ineligibility for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. Since Castro resigned one day before the judgment was finalized, the TSE did not annul his mandate but recognized the prejudiciality of the cassation. The decision opens the period for filing clarification appeals, while the determination of Rio’s interim succession — direct or indirect — remains under review at the STF.

item.title: Gilmar pede desculpas
item.description: Gilmar Mendes, dean of the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF), apologized for mentioning homosexuality while attempting to justify the inclusion of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, a pre-candidate for president, in the fake news inquiry. He denounced a supposed 'industry of defamation' against the Court and vowed to confront it. The statement arose amid controversy over the use of personal arguments in judicial decisions.

item.title: Proposta de Dino traz itens genéricos sobre STF e tira foco de reformas a curto prazo na corte
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino released a text advocating for a broad reform of the Judiciary as a solution to concrete problems, amid public debate over the conduct of STF ministers, including the proposal for a judicial code of ethics. His proposal emphasizes long-term structural shifts, shifting focus away from immediate reforms within the court.

item.title: Cúpula do PT exclui polêmicas de encontro do partido para evitar desgaste de Lula na pré-campanha
item.description: The PT leadership decided to exclude controversial topics from the party meeting's agenda this weekend to avoid further wear on President Lula ahead of the 2026 election campaign. The move aims to preserve the president's image and maintain focus on consensual themes during the pre-campaign period.

item.title: Publicação de acórdão do TSE aumenta pressão para Dino destravar julgamento sobre eleições no Rio
item.description: The TSE released the ruling that declared former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro ineligible, increasing pressure on Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino to rule on the case that will determine when and how new elections will be held in the state. As Brazil’s third-largest electoral college, the outcome of this case is critical for regional and national political stability.

item.title: TSE publica acórdão de julgamento que condenou Castro e diz que ex-governador não foi cassado
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) published the ruling that convicted former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) of abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections, rendering him ineligible until 2030. However, the TSE did not annul his mandate because he resigned before the judgment concluded, sparking allegations of a maneuver to avoid formal removal. Whether the interim election will be direct or indirect hinges on an ongoing interpretation by the Supreme Federal Court (STF).

item.title: TSE aprova repasse de R$ 13,2 milhões para Itamaraty organizar eleições no exterior
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously approved a R$13.2 million transfer to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Itamaraty) to organize the 2026 elections abroad, funding the rental of premises for 65 overseas voting sections where voter demand justifies expansion. The measure ensures the voting rights of Brazilians living overseas and complies with Electoral Code requirements, which mandate a minimum of 30 registered voters per section. Sections must be designated and reported to Itamaraty by July 6, 2026.

item.title: Gilmar cita ‘boneco de Zema como homossexual’ para reclamar de críticas ao STF: ‘Não é ofensivo?’
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes sparked controversy by suggesting that making a doll of Governor Romeu Zema as homosexual could be offensive, equating homosexuality with theft in the context of satire against the STF. After backlash, Mendes admitted the error and apologized, stating he did not intend to offend. Zema responded on social media, calling the remarks prejudiced and reaffirming his support for LGBTQIA+ causes with humor and an AI-generated image of himself holding a pride flag.

item.title: Zema diz que difere de Flávio por não buscar benefícios no Estado e volta a atacar STF
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) stated he differs from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) by not seeking personal benefits in the public sector. He also renewed his criticism of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) in an interview on RedeTV!'s É Notícia program. The remarks were made on April 23, 2026.

item.title: Gilmar recorre a série de entrevistas para rebater críticas e defender STF
item.description: Supreme Federal Court (STF) Minister Gilmar Mendes gave a series of press interviews to counter criticisms directed at the Court and defend his public positions. He sought to uphold the independence of the Judiciary and justify recent rulings that have faced political scrutiny. The interviews were broadcast on national media outlets and widely circulated until the morning of April 23, 2026.

item.title: Lula vai a SP para tirar excesso de pele na cabeça e tratar tendinite
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will undergo two simple medical procedures this Friday (24) at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital in São Paulo: removal of scalp keratose and an injection to treat tendinitis in the thumb of his right hand. The procedures do not require hospitalization, prior preparation, or rest, according to the government's Secretariat of Communication.
